rounds.text: Quess Corp Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 19.4x [E1] while delivering exceptional capital efficiency, evidenced by an ROE of 21.3% [E13] and an ROCE of 24.0% [E12], both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks of 4.86% and 6.56% respectively [E9, E10]. The company's underlying earnings power is robust and accelerating, with compounded profit growth jumping 39% over 5 years [E19] and 22% over the trailing twelve months [E21], alongside a stellar rules-based screen score of 87 out of 100 pointing to strong recent quarterly performance [E66, E68]. Furthermore, the business is exceptionally well-funded and cash-generative, boasting a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.11x [E38], full cash backing of reported profits at a 1.04x cash conversion rate [E34], and free cash flow of Rs 221 Cr as of March 2026 [E36], all while rewarding shareholders with a healthy dividend yield of 2.41% [E4]. Technical momentum solidly supports this fundamental strength, with the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages and sporting a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51, E52]. Conceded: [E16], [E23], [E43].

The bear case rests on deteriorating top-line momentum, structural institutional abandonment, and a history of brutal capital destruction. Compounded sales growth over the last 3 years has contracted to -4.5% [E16], and the 5-year sales growth is flagged as a poor 7.15% [E63]. Furthermore, foreign institutional investors have aggressively slashed their holdings from 16.93% in September 2023 to 8.58% in June 2026 [E43], contributing to negative institutional money flow [E45]. This lack of smart-money support is matched by extreme historical volatility [E55] and a catastrophic worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -86.9% [E54]. Compounded share price growth over a 5-year period remains negative at -5% [E23], while the stock trades at an elevated price-to-book multiple of 4.52x against a sector benchmark of just 1.44x [E7]. Conceded: the company maintains a robust ROCE of 21.61% compared to a sector benchmark of 6.56% [E10] and strong recent operating cash flows [E35].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over the last 3 years contracted by -4% [E16], and 5-year sales growth is cited as a poor 7.15% [E63]. However, top-line performance has sharply accelerated with a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 22% [E21], a 5-year compounded profit growth of 39% [E19], and recent quarterly screens showing sales up 15% YoY alongside net profit surging 61% YoY [E67, E68]. Conceded: foreign institutional holdings dropped to 8.58% [E43], but domestic institutions concurrently increased their stake to 11.86% [E44]. While the bear highlights historical drawdowns [E54], the stock currently trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with the 50-day above the 200-day [E51], alongside a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 [E52]. Finally, the elevated price-to-book ratio [E7] is fully justified by superior underlying returns, featuring an exceptional ROCE of 21.61% crushing the sector benchmark of 6.56% [E10] and fully cash-backed profits of Rs 230 Cr [E34, E35].

Conceded: TTM profit growth reached 22% [E21], and recent screens show net profit surging 61% YoY [E68]. However, that acceleration sits atop a concerning medium-term top-line contraction where 3-year compounded sales growth fell by -4% [E16] and 5-year growth lagged at a poor 7.15% [E63]. While the bull points to domestic institutions buying [E44], it glosses over the severe exodus of foreign institutional investors whose holdings collapsed from 16.93% to 8.58% alongside negative money flow signals [E43, E45]. Conceded: the stock trades above its moving averages [E51], but technical momentum fails to erase a staggering historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -86.9% paired with a weak Sharpe ratio of 0.19 [E54, E56]. Finally, dismissing the elevated price-to-book ratio [E7] via strong ROCE ignores explicit warnings flagging both the premium P/B multiple and a low multi-year return on equity of just 13.5% over the last 3 years [E62, E65].

Conceded: 3-year compounded sales growth contracted by -4% [E16]. However, this top-line lumpiness is completely overshadowed by aggressive profit compounding, where 5-year profit growth reached 39% and TTM profit growth hit 22% [E19, E21], proving that management has successfully optimized for high-margin execution over mere top-line expansion. While the bear laments foreign institutional departures [E43, E45], domestic institutions actively increased their stake to 11.86% [E44], reflecting strong local conviction in the underlying fundamentals. Conceded: historical drawdowns reached -86.9% [E54]. Yet, today's price action is fully supported by concrete metrics, sitting safely above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 [E51, E52]. Finally, dismissing the valuation through a multi-year ROE citation ignores the company's powerful, up-to-date performance, featuring a current ROCE of 24.0% and an ROE of 21.3% that vastly outpace sector benchmarks [E10, E12, E13].

Conceded: 5-year profit growth reached 39% [E19]. However, dismissing top-line deterioration by calling it mere lumpiness ignores the fact that 3-year compounded sales growth contracted by -4% and 5-year sales growth languishes at a poor 7% [E16, E63]. Furthermore, pointing to domestic institutional accumulation overlooks the severe structural exit of foreign institutions, whose stake plummeted from 16.93% to 8.58% alongside negative money flow signals [E43, E45]. While technical strength and moving averages look robust today [E51, E52], relying on them to downplay historical risk ignores the catastrophic record of an 86.9% peak-to-trough drawdown and an anemic Sharpe ratio of 0.19 [E54, E56]. Finally, the bull's appeal to modern ROE metrics masks a persistent vulnerability flagged in the statements: a low 3-year average return on equity of 13.5% and a rich price-to-book ratio of 4.52x against a sector benchmark of just 1.44x [E7, E62, E65].
